findings.title: Delete never appears in the ruler-less list view
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu now ORs Grafana Prometheus-rule abilities into canDelete so the list can authorize actions without a ruler fetch. The Delete item is still rendered only when rulerRule is set (`canDelete && rulerRule` at line 165). The new list (GrafanaRuleListItem → RuleActionsButtons) passes only promRule, so rulerRule is undefined and Delete is never shown, even for users with folder delete permission. The list click handler already ignores the ruler argument and opens the delete modal with the identifier built from the Prometheus rule uid, so this guard drops a primary action rather than protecting anything. GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx grants AlertingRuleDelete, defines a delete menu query, and then asserts exactly four menu items, so the regression stays green.

findings.title: Pause/resume is unreachable without a ruler rule
findings.body: The Pause item is still rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) is true, and MenuItemPauseRule is given that ruler rule. The new list never loads a ruler rule, so canPause computed from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is ignored. Users cannot pause or resume rules from the list, including rules whose paused state is already shown from the Prometheus payload (isPaused). MenuItemPauseRule still needs a RulerGrafanaRuleDTO to call the pause API, so the prom-rule ability check cannot drive the action until pause is implemented from the rule uid or the ruler rule is loaded on demand.

findings.title: Silence menu item is a no-op in the list view
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu renders "Silence notifications" from prom-rule abilities and does not require a ruler rule. handleSilence only sets showSilenceDrawer. The drawer is mounted only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true, and rule is the optional ruler rule, which the list view does not pass. Clicking Silence therefore closes the menu and does nothing. The new group-loader test asserts the menu item is present but never activates it, so the no-op is not caught. Silencing from the list needs a path that can run from the Grafana rule uid, or an on-demand ruler fetch before opening SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer.

findings.title: Federated rules are no longer immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to set isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and fold that into immutableRule, which blocks Update, Delete, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently. That body now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which only receives a RulerRuleDTO and RuleGroupIdentifierV2 (neither has source_tenants) and hardcodes isFederated to false. Every existing caller of useAlertRuleAbility / useAllAlertRuleAbilities — rule detail and the old rules table, not only the new list — will offer edit and delete on federated Mimir/GEM rules. Those mutations were blocked because saving the group without source_tenants can drop cross-tenant evaluation. The CombinedRule path still has rule.group and should keep the check even if the ruler-only hook cannot.

findings.title: skipToken still grants Duplicate via Grafana create permission
findings.body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken) is meant to skip the check for non-Grafana rules, but it calls useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). For a missing rule, useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading: false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported, and Duplicate is [true, user has getRulesPermissions('grafana').create]. AlertRuleMenu ORs that with the ruler result. On a cloud/datasource rule, a user who cannot duplicate external rules but can create Grafana-managed rules still sees Duplicate, and choosing it starts RedirectToCloneRule for that cloud rule. skipToken/undefined should be not-supported and not-allowed for every action. The OR also means any false allow on the prom side overrides a ruler denial.

findings.title: Filtered Grafana rules are rendered without a React key
findings.body: FilterViewResults maps rules and passes the computed key for datasource and unknown origins. The grafana branch previously rendered GrafanaRuleLoader with key={key} and now renders GrafanaRuleListItem with no key, even though key is still destructured specifically to avoid duplicate keys. React then reconciles Grafana rows by index. RuleActionsButtons holds silence-drawer and clone-redirect state, so load-more appends or a list update can attach that state to the wrong rule. Pass key={key} on GrafanaRuleListItem, matching the other branches.

findings.title: Recording rules lose export and pause in prom abilities
findings.body: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities uses prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule as the Grafana-managed check for ModifyExport, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently. Recording rules are Grafana-managed too (uid, folderUid, isPaused, provenance on the shared prom DTO). The ruler abilities this replaces used rulerRuleType.grafana.rule, which is true for recording rules, so the old list offered Export and Pause. The new list will not, while Edit and Delete are not gated this way. Silence should stay alerting-only; export, pause, restore, and permanent delete should follow "is a Grafana prom rule" plus the immutability checks, not alerting type.

findings.title: Rule view links drop returnTo
findings.body: The removed GrafanaRuleLoader built the view href with createReturnTo() so rule detail could navigate back to the current list URL, including filters and pagination. GrafanaRuleListItem now links to /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view with no returnTo query. Opening a rule from the filtered list and going back lands on the default list instead of the filtered results.
